covers: Wall Street's first session of Fed week and emerging markets, Monday 26 October 2026, to about 3:16 p.m. ET (21:16 SAST)
headline: Fitch says South Africa's debt will edge up again by 2029, as Brazil's sell-off deepens and Wall Street holds gains into the last hour
summary: Fitch kept a more cautious view than Treasury, expecting South Africa's debt to stabilise near 78% of GDP and then edge up to 79% in 2028-29 (BB, stable; next review 11 December), on the same day Moody's called the budget update credit positive (Daily Investor; Bloomberg, 26 Oct); Brazil's Bovespa fell nearly 17% and the real lost more than 10% after Lula's re-election (Quartz, 26 Oct), a shock that can spill over to the rand, which sat near R16.61/$ this morning (Reuters via Business Recorder, 06:02 GMT). Wall Street kept its gains into the last hour: at about 3:16 p.m. ET the S&P 500 was up 0.73% at 7,679.54, the Nasdaq up 0.97% at 26,207.79 and the Dow up 0.19% at 52,315.97, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.99% (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct); Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 staff two days before its results (TechCrunch, 26 Oct). Oil eased on Iran de-escalation talks, with WTI down 0.90% at $102.34, and gold rose 0.37% to $4,022.60 (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct, about 3:16 p.m. ET).

items.title: Brazil's sell-off deepens: Bovespa down nearly 17%, real off more than 10% after Lula wins; Bolsonaro rejects the result
items.summary: Lula won Sunday's run-off with 51.79% to Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.21%; Bolsonaro said he does not recognise the result and will seek to annul it (Rio Times; MercoPress, 26 Oct). After an opening trading halt, the Bovespa fell nearly 17% and the real lost more than 10% (Quartz, 26 Oct); Investing.com reported the real 12% weaker at 5.60 per dollar in early spot trade, against about 5.01 at the 23 October close (Investing.com; Seoul Economic Daily, 26 Oct). B3 widened the daily limit to 20% and the Treasury cancelled bond auctions for 27–29 October (MercoPress, 26 Oct). Investors worry about public debt above 82% of GDP and the lack of a concrete spending plan (Seoul Economic Daily, 26 Oct). Why it matters for SA: Brazil and South Africa are often traded together as emerging markets, so a Brazil shock can weigh on the rand and JSE.

items.title: Meta details $35 billion share sale, with up to $60 billion more planned from 2027
items.summary: Meta launched $22.5 billion of common stock via forward sales (cash drawn by 19 Nov 2027) plus $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred; it also plans up to $60 billion of Class C shares from Q1 2027, taking the possible total to $95 billion. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicated non-binding interest in up to $5 billion. Shares fell 1.7% in early trading after a $642.62 close on Friday (TIKR; TheStreet; FinanceFeeds, 26 Oct).

items.title: Moody's says South Africa's budget update is credit positive; no rating action
items.summary: In a report on Monday, Moody's said the medium-term budget policy statement is positive for South Africa's credit profile, citing continued fiscal consolidation despite higher oil prices. The FY2026 consolidated deficit target was cut to 3.9% of GDP from 4.0%, helped by a R17.1bn upward revision to tax revenue. Moody's sees government debt at 84.9% of GDP by FY2028, down from about 86.8% in FY2025, and says debt has 'probably peaked', though interest took 18.8% of revenue in FY2025. It also called the draft fiscal-rules law credit positive. South Africa stays at Ba2 with a positive outlook; Moody's did not announce a rating action (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 26 Oct).

items.title: Fitch expects South Africa's debt to edge up again by 2029, unlike Treasury; no rating action
items.summary: Fitch, which rates South Africa BB with a stable outlook after its June upgrade, expects government debt to stabilise at about 78% of GDP over the next two fiscal years and then rise to about 79% in 2028-29: 'unlike the government, we expect debt to GDP to very modestly rise again' (Daily Investor; Bloomberg, 26 Oct). Its next scheduled review is on 11 December. The view is more cautious than Moody's, which called the budget update credit positive earlier on Monday.

items.title: Oil falls as Saudi defence minister leads talks in Tehran
items.summary: Brent was down 1.34% at $115.20 and WTI down 1.78% at $101.40 at 7:17 a.m. ET on 26 Oct (TheStreet) as Saudi Arabia's defence minister led a delegation to regional de-escalation talks in Tehran (Kuwait Times, 26 Oct). Houthi attacks on Saudi sites keep supply risk high.

items.title: Wall Street holds gains into the last hour; Nasdaq up about 1%
items.summary: At about 3:16 p.m. ET the S&P 500 was up 0.73% at 7,679.54, the Nasdaq up 0.97% at 26,207.79 and the Dow up 0.19% at 52,315.97; the 10-year Treasury yield was 4.99% (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct). Chipmakers and AI hardware led after a large AI start-up filed for a Nasdaq IPO: Nvidia rose about 2.2%, Lumentum about 8–10% on a Buy initiation, and Tesla about 6% after a Barclays upgrade to overweight; Apple fell about 1.1% and the VIX fell 5.9% to 18.31 (Benzinga; Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct).

items.title: Brazil-linked US listings: EWZ heads for its worst day since March 2020
items.summary: At midday the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ) was down about 21.7%, broker XP down about 48% and Nu Holdings down about 19.5% (Benzinga, 26 Oct). Before the open EWZ had been down as much as 27.68% (TradingKey, 26 Oct).

items.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
items.summary: Microsoft is offering a 'Voluntary Exit Offer' to about 60,000 staff at vice-president level and below on selected teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK; data-centre, sales and marketing groups are excluded, and terms are similar to a standard severance package (TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg and Business Insider, 26 Oct). Earlier in 2026 more than 30% of about 8,750 eligible retirement-age staff took a buyout (TechCrunch). Microsoft shares were up 1.02% at $529.86 at about 11:30 a.m. ET (StreetInsider, 26 Oct). The company reports results on Wednesday.

items.title: EQT agrees all-stock deal for Range Resources, valued at about $50 billion
items.summary: Range Resources shares jumped about 15% after it agreed an all-stock merger with EQT valued at about $50 billion; Fair Isaac fell about 11% after holding its mortgage-score pricing flat (Benzinga, 26 Oct).

items.title: Verizon raises 2026 guidance after a strong quarter for phone customers
items.summary: Verizon reported third-quarter revenue of $34.3 billion (+1.5% year on year) and adjusted EPS of $1.31 (+8.3%), with 406,000 postpaid phone net additions. It raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.04–$5.06 (7.0%–7.5% growth) and now expects free cash flow growth near 12%, up from 9%–10%; capex guidance is unchanged at $16.0–16.5 billion (Verizon results filing, 26 Oct).

items.title: Neocloud stocks recover after early slide on Musk's 'guppy-level death' warning
items.summary: In pre-market trading on Monday, CoreWeave was down 2.7% and Nebius down 3.5% after Elon Musk posted that 200+ 'neocloud' data-centre firms face 'guppy-level death and consolidation' because lenders are reluctant to fund them; BofA's Tal Liani called the CoreWeave selloff sentiment-driven and kept his $140 target (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct). By late morning both had reversed their early losses to trade higher (Reuters, 26 Oct).

items.title: Busy week: Fed decision Wednesday, big tech results, GDP and PCE Thursday
items.summary: The Fed announces its decision on Wed 28 Oct at 18:00 GMT (20:00 SAST) and is expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00%. Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close on Wednesday, Amazon and Intel on Thursday. Q3 GDP (forecast 3.1% annualised) and core PCE (forecast +0.2% m/m) come out on Thursday, and the ECB (Thursday) and Bank of Japan (Friday) also decide on rates (Babypips, 26 Oct). Futures pricing (CME FedWatch) gives a 75% chance of a Fed hike in December (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct).

items.title: Musk says SpaceX closed a $40 billion debt deal for AI chips
items.summary: In a Sunday post on X, Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing, mainly for GPUs arriving in the first half of 2027. He warned that lenders have nearly stopped funding 'neocloud' data-centre firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius. The claim comes from Musk's post; no filing or lender statement has been cited (Yahoo Finance, 25 Oct).

items.title: Pick n Pay narrows its half-year loss as Boxer keeps growing
items.summary: For the six months to end-August, group turnover rose 2.4% to R60.5bn, with Boxer up 6.3%, the core Pick n Pay segment mostly flat and online sales up 35.4%. The headline loss narrowed to R299m from R439m a year earlier (40.71c a share from 59.77c), and group trading profit rose 58.1% to R490m (BusinessDay, 26 Oct). Pick n Pay is not a covered company.

items.title: Rand steady at about R16.61/$ ahead of the Fed and month-end data
items.summary: At 06:02 GMT the rand was at 16.6125 to the dollar, little changed from its previous close, and the 2035 bond yield was steady at 8.635% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct).

items.title: Stats SA to publish rebased GDP figures on Thursday
items.summary: This week Stats SA releases rebased and benchmarked GDP estimates and the September PPI on Thu 29 Oct; Nedbank expects PPI inflation to rise to 5.3% from 5.0%. SARS trade data for September follows on Friday, after August's R20.5bn surplus (Business Day, 26 Oct).

items.title: Oil eases on Iran talks; WTI around $102
items.summary: At about 3:16 p.m. ET WTI December crude was down 0.90% at $102.34 (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct); at midday Brent was near $111.84 (Benzinga, 26 Oct).

items.title: Brazil's real: more than 10% weaker
items.summary: The real lost more than 10% on Monday (Quartz, 26 Oct); Investing.com reported it 12% weaker at 5.60 per dollar in early spot trade, from about 5.01 at the 23 October close (Investing.com; Seoul Economic Daily, 26 Oct).

items.title: Gold up about 0.4% at $4,023 ahead of the Fed
items.summary: At about 3:16 p.m. ET gold was up $14.70 (0.37%) at $4,022.60 (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct); bitcoin was roughly flat near $80,000 at midday (Benzinga, 26 Oct).

items.title: META: shares steady after $35 billion share sale, up to $95 billion in total
items.summary: Meta's $35 billion stock sale (plus a planned $60 billion from 2027) dilutes existing holders to fund AI spending; shares fell 1.7% in early trade (TheStreet, 26 Oct) but were up about 0.2% by late morning (Reuters, 26 Oct). Results came on 21 Oct, when the stock was near $709. META is a BUY on the LRC Stock Scanner; rating unchanged.

items.title: NVIDIA: SpaceX says it has funding for a large AI-chip order
items.summary: Musk says SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt for GPUs (Yahoo Finance, 25 Oct). Earlier October reports said the money was for NVIDIA chips, but this has not been confirmed. If confirmed, it supports demand for NVIDIA (BUY on our list, LRC target $262.56). The other side: neocloud customers CoreWeave and Nebius fell about 3% before Monday's open after Musk warned lenders are pulling back from such firms (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct), a demand risk to watch; both had recovered to trade higher by late morning, and the Philadelphia chip index was up more than 3% (Reuters, 26 Oct). Rating unchanged. Nvidia, with AMD and Broadcom, also indicated non-binding interest in buying up to $5 billion of Meta's new shares (TIKR, 26 Oct).
